full_name: Monte Rei Golf & Country Club (North Course)

summary.text: Portugal's first Jack Nicklaus Signature course, and Nicklaus's only Portuguese design, set in the hills of the eastern Algarve.

setting.text: Sits in the foothills of the eastern Algarve, with views of the Serra do Caldeirão mountains to the north and the Atlantic to the south.
Laid out on an undulating plateau about 6km inland, near Tavira, on rocky ground the designers left largely with its natural humps and hollows.
The estate covers 1,000 acres of countryside around the course.
The back nine runs over lower ground on the southern side of the site and holds the most picturesque holes.
Long distances between greens and tees make it a buggy course; it can be walked, but the hikes make for a long day.

history.text: Opened in summer 2007; an early visitor wrote it had been open only six weeks when he played it in late August 2007.
The masterplan envisaged two Nicklaus Signature courses; the planned South course has yet to be built.
Monte Rei announced plans for the second Nicklaus course in 2019; it has not yet been built.
Asset manager Arrow Global bought the club in January 2025; it is run by Portuguese firm Details.
Closed from April 2026 for a six-month renovation with Nicklaus Design: greens rebuilt, bunkers upgraded, irrigation and pump station renewed, cart paths refurbished.
The renovation also restored areas affected by recent fires.
Reopened in September 2026. Nicklaus Design's Dirk Bouts said many tees were enlarged and the work set out to restore the course to Jack's original design, not reinvent it.

trivia.text: Held No.1 in Top100golfcourses' Portugal ranking for fifteen years until the 2026 update, when Terras da Comporta (Dunas) displaced it to No.2.
Top100golfcourses ranks it 13th in Continental Europe and 1st in the Algarve.
Water comes into play on eleven of the eighteen holes.
Five par 3s, five par 5s and eight par 4s; over 7,200 yards from the back tees.
Offset greens tucked behind water or huge bunkers, leaving a safer 'dry side', are a recurring Nicklaus ploy here.
A 100-room Nobu hotel, signature restaurant and branded residences are planned for the resort.

1.text: Opens with a par 4 from an elevated tee to a fairway that doglegs right, with huge bunkers off the tee and at the green.

3.text: The green sits tucked behind just enough water to leave a safer shot to the dry side.

6.text: Huge, intimidating bunkers stand in for water in front of an offset green.

7.text: The toughest of a strong set of par 3s: over 230 yards from the back tee, with only a narrow channel onto the green and deep hollows either side.

8.text: Like the 6th, a par 5 where huge bunkers guard an offset green in place of water.

9.text: A pretty drop-shot par 3 to a canted green benched into the hill, ringed by artistic bunkering; the one short hole that offers respite.

12.text: A horseshoe par 4 around water: long hitters can try to drive the green, everyone else lays up and wedges on.

13.text: The signature hole: a downhill par 4 cascading from an elevated tee down a natural valley, with two bunkers in the fairway.
The green sits on a promontory jutting into the lake, behind a severe false front that sends balls back to the player's feet.
Even with an approach under 100 yards, a par here is a great achievement.
Often called the most photographed hole on the course.

14.text: Probably the prettiest hole: a mid-length par 3 across the corner of a lake, where anything pulled left finds 'a watery grave'.
The green is set diagonally with the pond tight to its left edge; with a left pin the tee shot is very intimidating.

15.text: A mid-length par 4 that follows a lake all the way from tee to green.

16.text: A par 5 with lots of fairway bunkers and a creek cutting the fairway that forces shorter hitters to lay up.

18.text: A shorter par 5 that curls round a lake to the green; in reach in two for the biggest hitters, with the lake in play on everyone's second and third.
A reviewer called going for it in two over the water 'a real dilemma' and their birdie there a golfing highlight.

local.text: Lies in the hills north-east of Tavira, towards the Spanish border, away from the cluster of courses around Albufeira.
The club's address is Sesmarias, Vila Nova de Cacela.
